---
title: "Wesley"
format: html
---
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
dataset <- load("data/wrangledData.Rdata")
```

```{r}
division3_football <- filter(division3, ClassificationCode == 6)
nrow(division3_football)
```
```{r}

spending_data <- bind_rows(division1, division3_football)

nrow(spending_data)
```
```{r}

# Creating new column that will be used to group schools in our summary table.

spending_data <- mutate(
  spending_data,
  division_label = ifelse(
    ClassificationCode == 1,
    "Division I-FBS",
    "Division III with Football"
  )
)

```

```{r}

summary_table <- summarise(
  group_by(spending_data, division_label),
  schools = n(),
  median_spending_ratio = median(spending_ratio)
)

summary_table
```
```{r}

# A spending ratio greater than 1 means men's programs
# receive more spending than women's programs.
# A spending ratio less than 1 means women's programs
# receive more spending than men's programs.
# A ratio equal to 1 means both receive the same amount.


spending_data <- mutate(
  spending_data,
  spending_direction = ifelse(
    spending_ratio > 1,
    "Higher spending on men",
    ifelse(
      spending_ratio < 1,
      "Higher spending on women",
      "Equal spending"
    )
  )
)
```

```{r}
# Comparing institutional gender spending ratios between
# NCAA Division I-FBS and Division III with football.
#
# Each point represents one institution.
# Pink points show higher spending on women's programs.
# Blue points show higher spending on men's programs.
# The dashed horizontal line at 1 indicates equal spending.
# Black diamonds show the median ratio for each division.

ggplot(spending_data,
       aes(x = division_label, y = spending_ratio,
           color = spending_direction)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(
    data = summary_table,
    aes(x = division_label, y = median_spending_ratio),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 18,
    size = 4,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Higher spending on men" = "steelblue",
      "Higher spending on women" = "deeppink",
      "Equal spending" = "gray50"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gender Spending Ratios Across NCAA Divisions",
    x = "NCAA Division",
    y = "Men's-to-Women's Spending Ratio",
    color = "Spending Direction"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
